subproblems.title: Sub-ball consequences of the Allard hypotheses (K-monotonicity, finite curvature integral, mass bound)
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers and p a real number with n < p. Let U be a subset of R^(n+l), V a RectifiableVarifold n l U with weight mu = V.weight, H : R^(n+l) -> R^(n+l), and delta, rho real numbers such that V.AllardHypotheses H p delta rho holds. Then for every z in R^(n+l) and every r with 0 < r <= rho and closed ball B_r(z) contained in B_rho(0): (a) B_r(z) is contained in U; (b) the lower integral of |H|^p over B_r(z) with respect to mu is finite; (c) K(z,r) := (r^(p-n) * integral^-_{B_r(z)} |H|^p dmu)^(1/p) <= delta (as an element of [0,infinity], i.e. V.scaledLpNorm H p z r <= ofReal delta); (d) mu(B_r(z)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n rho^n (as ofReal).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (p : ℝ), (n : ℝ) < p → ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (δ ρ : ℝ), V.AllardHypotheses H p δ ρ → ∀ (z : Amb n ℓ) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → r ≤ ρ → closedBall z r ⊆ closedBall 0 ρ → closedBall z r ⊆ U ∧ ∫⁻ x in closedBall z r, ‖H x‖ₑ ^ p ∂V.weight < ⊤ ∧ V.scaledLpNorm H p z r ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ ∧ V.weight (closedBall z r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + δ) * (unitBallVolume n * ρ ^ n))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted declaration: Submission.aal_allard_subball_bounds. It is DAG node root.affine_approximation-a1.pinched_density_bounds-a1.allard_subball_bounds-a1, status accepted, with reviewed candidate commit 595bf34cad5e797b1ca2c89a3d419f3daecdab75 (isolated comparator passed). The frozen Lean type is byte-identical to that node's, so the controller maps this child to the existing accepted node and creates no new proof work. The numbered proof below is that node's independently approved proof, copied verbatim; in it, 'the parent proof' means that node's own parent (root.affine_approximation-a1.pinched_density_bounds-a1).

Use in the present parent (lip_approx_monotonicity), whose hypotheses include V.AllardHypotheses H p delta rho, p > n and 4 p delta/(p - n) <= Lambda. For a closed ball B_r(z) contained in B_rho(0) with r > 0, the parent first gets |z| + r <= rho, hence r <= rho (the point z + (r/|z|) z, or r e for a unit vector e when z = 0, lies in B_r(z) and therefore in B_rho(0); for z = y this is step (0a)). This child then applies with the parent's U, V, H, delta, rho:
- step (0c): (d) gives mu(B_r(z)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n rho^n < infinity, and (a) gives B_r(z) contained in U, so H is mu-integrable on the compact ball B_r(z) by the local integrability in HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature;
- step 2: (a) at (z, R_z) gives tsupport X_t contained in B_((1+eps)t)(z), a subset of B_(R_z)(z), a subset of U;
- step 4: (b) at (z, R_z) gives integral over B_(R_z)(z) of |H|^p dmu < infinity, so Hoelder's inequality applies;
- step 9: (c) at (y, R) gives K(y,R) <= delta <= ((p - n)/(4p)) Lambda, because 4 p delta/(p - n) <= Lambda; this is the smallness hypothesis K(z,R_z) <= kappa Lambda_z of steps 1-8 at z = y, R_z = R, Lambda_z = Lambda.
The scaled bound K(z,t) <= (t/rho)^(1-n/p) delta of step (0b), needed in step 10 so that Lambda_tau -> 0, is not part of this child; the parent proves it by the same domain monotonicity with the extra factor t^(p-n) = (t/rho)^(p-n) rho^(p-n).

Copied approved proof:
Source: the items (K-mono) and (A) of the notation section of the parent proof, and the facts derived from them in step 3 of the parent proof (B_S(y) in U, finiteness of the |H|^p integral over B_S(y), K(y,R) <= delta, mu(B_R(y)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n rho^n), stated for a general sub-ball B_r(z) of B_rho(0).

Notation: mu := V.weight, B_s(w) := closedBall w s, I(w,s) := integral^-_{B_s(w)} ||H(x)||_e^p dmu(x) in [0,infinity], and K(w,s) := V.scaledLpNorm H p w s = (ofReal(s^(p-n)) * I(w,s))^(1/p) in [0,infinity].

1. By definition, V.AllardHypotheses H p delta rho contains: rho > 0, B_rho(0) contained in U, mu(B_rho(0)) <= ofReal((1 + delta)(omega_n rho^n)), and K(0,rho) <= ofReal(delta). (Its remaining components - generalized mean curvature, theta >= 1 mu-a.e., 0 in spt V - are not needed here.) Since n >= 0 and p > n we have p > 0, 1/p > 0 and p - n > 0.

2. (a) B_r(z) is contained in B_rho(0), which is contained in U.

3. (d) By monotonicity of the measure mu, mu(B_r(z)) <= mu(B_rho(0)) <= ofReal((1 + delta)(omega_n rho^n)).

4. Since B_r(z) is contained in B_rho(0) and the integrand is nonnegative, monotonicity of the lower Lebesgue integral in the domain gives I(z,r) <= I(0,rho).

5. (c) (K-mono) Since 0 < r <= rho and p - n >= 0, r^(p-n) <= rho^(p-n), hence ofReal(r^(p-n)) <= ofReal(rho^(p-n)). Together with step 4 and monotonicity of multiplication in [0,infinity], ofReal(r^(p-n)) I(z,r) <= ofReal(rho^(p-n)) I(0,rho). Since 1/p >= 0, the map x -> x^(1/p) is monotone on [0,infinity], so K(z,r) <= K(0,rho) <= ofReal(delta).

6. (b) We have K(0,rho) <= ofReal(delta) < infinity. If ofReal(rho^(p-n)) I(0,rho) were infinite, then K(0,rho) = infinity^(1/p) = infinity because 1/p > 0, a contradiction; so ofReal(rho^(p-n)) I(0,rho) < infinity. As rho > 0, rho^(p-n) > 0, so ofReal(rho^(p-n)) is nonzero; a product in [0,infinity] whose first factor is nonzero and whose second factor is infinite is infinite, hence I(0,rho) < infinity. By step 4, I(z,r) <= I(0,rho) < infinity, which is (b).
proof_key_steps: Unpack rho > 0, B_rho(0) in U, the mass bound and K(0,rho) <= delta from AllardHypotheses; p > n >= 0 gives p > 0.
Ball inclusion gives (a) directly and (d) by monotonicity of mu.
r^(p-n) <= rho^(p-n), domain monotonicity of the lower integral and monotonicity of x^(1/p) give K(z,r) <= K(0,rho) <= delta.
K(0,rho) < infinity and rho^(p-n) > 0 force integral^-_{B_rho(0)} |H|^p < infinity, hence the integral over B_r(z) is finite.

subproblems.title: Radial first-variation identity for the cutoff fields phi(|x-y|/rho)(x-y) (Simon Ch. 4, 3.2-3.3 and 4.1)
subproblems.statement: Let n, l >= 0 be integers, U a subset of R^(n+l), and V a RectifiableVarifold n l U with generalized mean curvature H in U (V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H). Let mu := V.weight and p_x := V.tangentProj x, and assume that for mu-a.e. x there is an n-dimensional subspace P of R^(n+l) such that p_x is the orthogonal projection onto P. Let y in R^(n+l), let phi : R -> R be C^1 with phi(t) = 1 for all t <= 1 and phi(t) = 0 for all t >= T, and let rho > 0 with the closed ball B_{T rho}(y) contained in U. Then, writing r = |x - y| and using the convention a/0 = 0, integral [n phi(r/rho) + (r/rho) phi'(r/rho) (1 - |x - y - p_x(x - y)|^2 / |x - y|^2)] dmu(x) = - integral phi(r/rho) (x - y).H(x) dmu(x), both sides being Bochner integrals over R^(n+l).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ), V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H → (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, ∃ P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ P = n ∧ V.tangentProj x = P.starProjection) → ∀ (y : Amb n ℓ) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (T ρ : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → (∀ t : ℝ, t ≤ 1 → φ t = 1) → (∀ t : ℝ, T ≤ t → φ t = 0) → 0 < ρ → closedBall y (T * ρ) ⊆ U → ∫ x, ((n : ℝ) * φ (‖x - y‖ / ρ) + ‖x - y‖ / ρ * deriv φ (‖x - y‖ / ρ) * (1 - ‖(x - y) - V.tangentProj x (x - y)‖ ^ 2 / ‖x - y‖ ^ 2)) ∂V.weight = -∫ x, φ (‖x - y‖ / ρ) * inner ℝ (x - y) (H x) ∂V.weight

Use in the present parent (lip_approx_monotonicity): it is steps 2-3 of the supplied proof (radial test field, divergence computation and first variation). For a centre z and radius R_z > 0 with B_(R_z)(z) contained in B_rho(0), the cutoff profile phi of step 1 (C^1, phi = 1 on (-infinity, 1], phi = 0 on [1+eps, infinity)) and t in (0, R_z/(1+eps)), apply it with y := z, phi := phi, T := 1 + eps and rho := t. Its hypotheses are:
- V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H, a component of AllardHypotheses;
- for mu-a.e. x, p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace: step (0d), from the frozen sibling dependency lip_approx_tangent_structure (its third conjunct);
- t > 0;
- B_((1+eps)t)(z) contained in B_(R_z)(z) contained in U: child allard_subball_bounds (a).
Its conclusion is integral [n phi(r/t) + (r/t) phi'(r/t)(1 - g(x))] dmu = - integral phi(r/t) <x - z, H(x)> dmu, with r = |x - z| and g(x) = |(x - z) - p_x(x - z)|^2/|x - z|^2 (g(z) = 0). This is step 3's identity integral div_M X_t dmu = - integral <X_t, H> dmu, with div_M X_t computed as in step 2. Since (r/t) phi'(r/t) = -t psi_t(x), and phi, psi_t, psi_t g are bounded and vanish off B_(R_z)(z), which has finite mu-measure, the left side splits as n I(t) - t I'(t) + t J'(t), with I' and J' as in step 1. The right side is -t^(n+1) e(t). This is (3.1). The differentiability of I and J and that rewriting stay in the parent.

Copied approved proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 4, 3.2-3.3 and 4.1. This is the first half of Step 2 of the parent proof, carried out for an arbitrary C^1 profile phi.
Notation: r(x) := |x - y|; for x != y, nu(x) := (x - y)/r(x). B_s(y) is the closed ball, B^o_s(y) the open ball.

1. The field X. Put X(x) := phi(r(x)/rho)(x - y). The open sets O_1 := {x : x != y} and O_2 := B^o_rho(y) cover R^(n+l).
 - On O_1, x -> |x - y| is C^infinity, since the Euclidean norm is smooth away from 0. So x -> phi(|x - y|/rho) is C^1, and X, its product with the affine map x -> x - y, is C^1 on O_1.
 - On O_2, r(x)/rho < 1, so phi(r(x)/rho) = 1 and X(x) = x - y. Thus X is smooth on O_2.
 Being C^1 is a local property, so X is C^1 on R^(n+l).

2. Support and admissibility. If X(x) != 0, then phi(r(x)/rho) != 0. So r(x)/rho < T, i.e. |x - y| < T rho. Hence the support of X lies in B^o_{T rho}(y), and tsupport X lies in its closure. That closure is contained in B_{T rho}(y), which is contained in U by hypothesis. tsupport X is closed and bounded, hence compact, so X has compact support. X is therefore admissible in the definition of V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H, which gives
 integral div_M X dmu = - integral X . H dmu, (A.1)
 where div_M X(x) = trace(DX(x) o p_x) (this is V.divM X x).

3. Right side. For every x, X(x) . H(x) = phi(r(x)/rho)(x - y) . H(x). So the right side of (A.1) is - integral phi(r/rho)(x - y) . H dmu.

4. Derivative of X.
 - For x in O_2 (in particular x = y), X agrees near x with v -> v - y, so DX(x) = id.
 - For x != y, write r = r(x) > 0. Then D(|. - y|)(x) v = nu . v, and the chain and product rules give
 DX(x) v = phi(r/rho) v + rho^(-1) phi'(r/rho) (nu . v)(x - y).

5. Linear algebra. Let P be an n-dimensional subspace and p the orthogonal projection onto P, so p is self-adjoint and idempotent.
 - trace p = dim P = n.
 - For vectors a, b, the map v -> (a . p v) b has trace a . p b. Indeed, the trace of v -> (c . v) b is c . b; take c = p a and use a . p v = p a . v.
 - For every vector u, u . p u = |p u|^2.
 - |u|^2 = |p u|^2 + |u - p u|^2, by Pythagoras, since p u is orthogonal to u - p u.

6. Divergence. By hypothesis there is a mu-conull set on which p_x is the orthogonal projection p onto some n-dimensional subspace, as in step 5. Fix x in that set.
 - Case x != y. By steps 4 and 5,
 div_M X(x) = phi(r/rho) trace p + rho^(-1) phi'(r/rho) nu . p(x - y)
 = n phi(r/rho) + rho^(-1) phi'(r/rho) r^(-1) |p(x - y)|^2
 = n phi(r/rho) + (r/rho) phi'(r/rho) |p(x - y)|^2 / r^2.
 Pythagoras with u = x - y gives |p(x - y)|^2 / r^2 = 1 - |x - y - p(x - y)|^2 / |x - y|^2.
 - Case x = y. Here DX(y) = id, so div_M X(y) = trace p = n. This equals the integrand at x = y: phi(0) = 1, and the second term carries the factor |x - y|/rho = 0.

7. Conclusion. By step 6, div_M X equals mu-a.e. the integrand
 n phi(r/rho) + (r/rho) phi'(r/rho)(1 - |x - y - p_x(x - y)|^2 / |x - y|^2).
 Integrals of mu-a.e. equal functions coincide. So (A.1) together with step 3 is exactly the asserted identity.
proof_key_steps: X(x) = phi(|x-y|/rho)(x-y) is C^1: it is smooth on {x != y}, and equals x - y on B^o_rho(y) because phi = 1 on (-infinity, 1].
X vanishes outside B^o_{T rho}(y), so tsupport X lies in B_{T rho}(y), a compact subset of U. Hence X is admissible: integral div_M X dmu = - integral phi(r/rho)(x - y).H dmu.
DX = id near y. For x != y, DX(x) = phi(r/rho) id + rho^(-1) phi'(r/rho) (nu tensor (x - y)).

At mu-a.e. x, p_x is a rank-n orthogonal projection p. Then trace p = n, the rank-one part has trace rho^(-1) phi' r^(-1) |p(x-y)|^2, and Pythagoras gives div_M X = n phi + (r/rho) phi' (1 - |x-y-p_x(x-y)|^2/|x-y|^2). At x = y, div_M X = n.
Integrals of mu-a.e. equal functions coincide, which yields the identity.

subproblems.title: A monotone density quantity with F -> 1 and lower density omega is at least omega (step 5 of the parent)
subproblems.statement: Let n be a natural number, alpha, omega, R, Lambda real numbers with alpha > 0, omega > 0, R > 0, and m, F : R -> R. Put Phi(u) := F(u) (m(u)/u^n) + (F(u) - 1). Assume (H1) |F(u) - 1| <= Lambda (u/R)^alpha for every u in (0, R]; (H2) Phi(u) <= Phi(t) whenever 0 < u <= t <= R; (H3) for every epsilon > 0, (1 - epsilon)(omega u^n) <= m(u) for all sufficiently small u > 0 (eventually along the filter u -> 0+). Then omega <= Phi(t) for every t in (0, R].

Use in the present parent (lip_approx_monotonicity): it is the limit statement of step 11, 'Taking liminf as t -> 0 and using step 10: Phi(s) >= omega_n'. Fix one cutoff eps in (0,1] with (1+eps) s < R and the objects of steps 1-7 at z = y, R_z = R, Lambda_z = Lambda: the cutoff mass I and the integrating factor F, with Phi(u) = F(u) u^-n I(u) + F(u) - 1. Apply this child with n := n, alpha := 1 - n/p > 0 (as p > n), omega := omega_n = unitBallVolume n > 0, R := s, Lambda := Lambda, m := I and F := F:
- (H1) by (5.1), |F(u) - 1| <= Lambda (u/R)^(1-n/p) <= Lambda (u/s)^(1-n/p) for 0 < u <= s < R (Lambda >= 0, and u/R <= u/s with a nonnegative exponent);
- (H2) by (5.2), Phi is nondecreasing on (0, R/(1+eps)), which contains (0, s];
- (H3) by step 10 at w = y (y is in spt V and |y| < rho by (0a)): liminf_(u -> 0+) u^-n mu(B_u(y)) >= omega_n, so for every eps' > 0 eventually (1 - eps') omega_n u^n <= mu(B_u(y)) <= I(u), the last inequality from 1_[0,1] <= phi in step 8.
The conclusion at t = s is omega_n <= F(s) (I(s)/s^n) + (F(s) - 1) = Phi(s); the rest of step 11 (F(s) s^-n I(s) >= omega_n - Lambda, division by F(s) <= e^(Lambda/2), the case omega_n <= Lambda, and eps -> 0) stays in the parent.

Copied approved proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof ('Letting u -> 0+ and then epsilon -> 0+ gives Phi(t) >= omega_n for every t in (0, R]'), abstracted from Phi(t) = F(t) t^(-n) mu(B_t(y)) + F(t) - 1 with m(u) = mu(B_u(y)) and alpha = 1 - n/p; the two limits are carried out simultaneously with epsilon = eta.

1. As u -> 0+, Lambda (u/R)^alpha -> 0. Indeed u -> u/R is continuous and vanishes at u = 0, and x -> x^alpha is continuous at x = 0 because alpha > 0, with 0^alpha = 0; hence Lambda (u/R)^alpha -> Lambda * 0 = 0 as u -> 0, in particular as u -> 0+.

2. Fix t with 0 < t <= R and suppose, for a contradiction, that Phi(t) < omega. Put d := omega - Phi(t) > 0 and eta := min{1/2, d/(2(2 omega + 1))}. Then 0 < eta <= 1/2 and eta (2 omega + 1) <= d/2.

3. Each of the following three conditions holds for all sufficiently small u > 0: u < t (because t > 0); Lambda (u/R)^alpha < eta (by step 1, since eta > 0); (1 - eta)(omega u^n) <= m(u) (by (H3) with epsilon = eta > 0). Since the filter of right neighbourhoods of 0 is proper, there is u > 0 satisfying all three.

4. Since 0 < u < t <= R, (H1) gives |F(u) - 1| <= Lambda (u/R)^alpha < eta. Hence F(u) > 1 - eta >= 1/2 > 0 and F(u) - 1 > -eta.

5. Since u^n > 0, dividing (1 - eta) omega u^n <= m(u) by u^n gives m(u)/u^n >= (1 - eta) omega, and (1 - eta) omega >= 0. Multiplying the inequalities F(u) >= 1 - eta >= 0 and m(u)/u^n >= (1 - eta) omega >= 0 gives F(u) (m(u)/u^n) >= (1 - eta)^2 omega.

6. Therefore Phi(u) = F(u)(m(u)/u^n) + (F(u) - 1) >= (1 - eta)^2 omega - eta >= (1 - 2 eta) omega - eta = omega - eta (2 omega + 1) >= omega - d/2 > omega - d = Phi(t), using (1 - eta)^2 >= 1 - 2 eta and omega > 0.

7. On the other hand 0 < u <= t <= R, so (H2) gives Phi(u) <= Phi(t), contradicting step 6. Hence Phi(t) >= omega. As t in (0, R] was arbitrary, the claim follows.
proof_key_steps: Assume Phi(t) < omega and set eta = min{1/2, (omega - Phi(t))/(2(2 omega + 1))}.
Choose small u in (0, t) with Lambda (u/R)^alpha < eta and m(u) >= (1 - eta) omega u^n.
Then F(u) >= 1 - eta > 0, so Phi(u) >= (1 - eta)^2 omega - eta > Phi(t).
This contradicts the monotonicity Phi(u) <= Phi(t).
